item.text: {"question_id":"3B.5","answer":"Tshisekedi’s exceptional security powers were administered broadly and only partly reviewed or narrowed. The state of siege was extended more than 50 times in 2023-era reporting, transferred civilian administration to military and police authorities, subjected civilians to military courts, and was assessed by Amnesty as violating constitutional and international human-rights requirements; the supplied evidence also reports no meaningful public debate on the extensions and no required international derogation notification (BATCH-0012-R03-E001; BATCH-0012-R03-E003; BATCH-0009-E002; BATCH-0015-E007). Its application was associated with systematic rights restrictions, harassment and imprisonment of journalists, mass pretrial detention, serious security-force abuses, and worsening civilian attacks and displacement, although the casualty and displacement figures span 2021 onward and do not establish that every abuse was personally ordered by Tshisekedi (BATCH-0009-E002; BATCH-0012-R03-E003). A qualifying corrective step was Tshisekedi’s August roundtable to consider maintaining, requalifying, or lifting the regime, followed by an October announcement of gradual easing, including ending a curfew and allowing peaceful demonstrations; the supplied evidence does not establish the roundtable’s recommendations, full implementation, repeal, or effective remedy by year-end (BATCH-0007-E002; BATCH-0021-E012; BATCH-0008-E007). Separately, the revised 2023 press law retained prison exposure for press offenses, and authorities detained and prosecuted journalist Stanis Bujakera under the digital code, press law, and penal code; these materials do not establish that surveillance or anti-terror provisions were the operative legal basis or that Tshisekedi ordered the case (BATCH-0025-E007; BATCH-0025-E012).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0012-R03-E001","BATCH-0012-R03-E003","BATCH-0009-E002","BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0007-E002","BATCH-0021-E012","BATCH-0008-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The complete legal text, legislative review, safeguards, and geographic scope of each extension are not supplied.","The evidence does not establish the precise presidential role in every detention, prosecution, or security-force abuse.","The roundtable’s outcome, the extent of implementation of the announced easing, repeal timing, and effective remedies by year-end are not established.","The counterfactual security effect of the state of siege cannot be measured confidently.","The supplied evidence does not substantiate a claim that surveillance or anti-terror provisions enabled the cited prosecutions."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported claim that surveillance and anti-terror provisions enabled journalist and critic prosecutions.","Qualified the Bujakera evidence as involving the digital code, press law, and penal code, without attributing the prosecution order to Tshisekedi.","Kept the favorable review and easing evidence while stating that implementation and remedy are unproven.","Preserved the temporal limitation that casualty and displacement figures cover the period since 2021."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["The legal texts and review records could clarify whether extensions satisfied domestic and international requirements.","Evidence on the actual implementation of the announced easing or later repeal could materially change the assessment.","Independent evidence on remedies, prosecutions of security-force personnel, and the security effects of the state of siege remains incomplete."]}
